lyrics:
[Intro: count-in shout, acoustic guitar strum, handclaps]
Five, six, seven, go

[Verse 1: quick, bright, synth bass and drums]
My baby still laughs at the jokes I tell
She knows them all by heart and she laughs as well
But there's a little pause before the laugh comes in
And I've been living in that pause since I don't know when

[Chorus: stacked voices, claps on every answer]
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're lonely
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're only here for the beat
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Look at all those hands

[Verse 2: quick, a little quieter underneath]
We built a life from a list on the fridge
Paint and a mortgage and a dog named Midge
Everything's working and the lawn is green
So what's this draught coming in between?

[Aside: spoken, band keeps going]
Is anybody hearing the words?
No? Okay.
Clap

[Chorus: stacked voices, claps on every answer]
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're lonely
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're only here for the beat
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Look at all those hands

[Breakdown: drums and bass only, call and response]
Left side of the room (present)
Right side of the room (present)
Hands up if the house is quiet
(Every single night)
Hands up if the house is quiet
(Every single night)

[Bridge: playful instruction, claps and organ]
Now wind it like a disposable camera
Wind it, wind it
Wind it like a disposable camera
Wind it, wind it
And flash

[Final Chorus: everything, whoops, organ on top]
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're lonely
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Clap if you're only here for the beat
Hey, clap (clap, clap)
Look at all those hands
Look at all those hands

[Outro: guitar strum and claps, voices drop out one by one]
Clap
Clap
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 159 BPM, 4/4 with one short two-beat bar in each cycle, so the pattern trips forward. G major. A sprint, bright and unstoppable.

VOICE: Male tenor, elastic and playful, sliding between singing, shouting and a comic spoken aside. Backing vocals are the same voice stacked many times, plus a group of men and women for the call-and-response.

INSTRUMENTS: A hard-strummed acoustic guitar leading the track. Constant handclaps. A buzzing, rubbery synth bass. A simple, dry, fast drum kit. A cheap-sounding combo organ. Squiggly synth fills. No electric guitar solo.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, a shouted count and the strum with claps. 0:07 Verse 1. 0:27 Chorus 1. 0:47 Verse 2. 1:07 Aside, three spoken lines over the groove. 1:17 Chorus 2. 1:37 Instrumental with organ. 1:52 Breakdown, drums and bass with call-and-response. 2:17 Bridge, the camera instruction. 2:42 Final chorus with whoops. 3:12 Outro, the voices drop out until only strum and claps remain, ending at 3:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s genre-blur made to sound like a 1960s TV performance through modern speakers: dry, bright, mono-ish drums, voices crowded together.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The spoken aside at 1:07, when the singer checks whether anyone is listening and then gives up.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The couple are settled, with a mortgage and a dog. The question is no longer whether love lasts but what a full, quiet house means. The obsolete gadget is now a disposable camera.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Cheer, a crack in it, a shrug, and louder cheer.
